title: Command Best Practices & Smells
body:
# Command Best Practices & Smells

## The thin adapter rule

```rust
// GOOD: parse → delegate → map error
#[tauri::command]
async fn complete_lesson(
    state: State<'_, AppState>,
    track_id: String,
    module_id: String,
    lesson_id: String,
) -> AppResult<ProgressSummary> {
    let catalog = content::load_catalog()?;
    let lesson = find_lesson(&catalog, &track_id, &module_id, &lesson_id)?; // validate
    let conn = lock_db(&state.db)?;
    repo::complete_lesson(&conn, &track_id, &lesson.module_id, &lesson.id)?;
    engine::summarize(&catalog, &repo::list_completed(&conn)?, &[…])
}
```

SQL, subprocess spawning and unlock rules live in services/engines — commands
would work equally well over HTTP or a test harness.

## Validate like the frontend is hostile (it is)

Every command in this app checks: string lengths, enum membership, id existence
against the catalog, numeric ranges. A compromised webview is inside your trust
boundary's *outside*.

## Smell: business logic in command handlers

If a command body exceeds ~10 lines of orchestration, logic is leaking up.
**Why:** untestable without launching Tauri; duplicated across commands.
**Refactor:** extract `service::do_thing(conn, args)`; unit-test that.

## Smell: trusting frontend input

`save_note(note)` once accepted any `scope_type`. Now it validates against a
closed set — because arbitrary strings eventually reach SQL LIKE clauses or
log injection. Closed enums > open strings at boundaries.

## Smell: excessive IPC chatter

Polling stores every 100 ms for data the backend could push (or compute once)
floods the bridge. This app batches startup into ONE `get_bootstrap` call.
